newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela pay offer won't boost inflation - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela pay offer won't boost inflation - Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuela's latest 35 percent across-the-board public sector pay rise offer will not bust the budget and does not threaten the government's inflation target for 1997, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
"(It) will not cause an increase in public spending and is compatible with the 25 to 30 percent inflation target we are using," Petkoff said Wednesday in a presentation to Congress.
In the government's 7.8 trillion bolivar ($16.4 billion) spending plans for the year, 1.2 trillion bolivars ($2.5 billion) has been earmarked for public sector pay increases, Petkoff said.
Although the hikes were originally slated at 25 percent, ministers have repeatedly said if pay rises top 1.2 trillion bolivars, cuts will have to be made elsewhere in the budget.
Nevertheless, analysts believe rising domestic demand on the back of the pay rises and a growing economy will boost inflation for the year to upwards of 35 percent.
Extrapolating over the year from January's 2.6 percent monthly rate would take 1997 inflation to over 40 percent, they say.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar announced earlier Wednesday the government had reached a preliminary accord with Venezuela's largest public sector union, the Confederation of Venezuelan workers (CTV), over the 35 percent pay offer that will also be topped-up with monthly bonuses.
The agreement came after nearly two months of strikes and strident public debate, but must still be cleared with other unions.
